name: אֱלִיצוּר
summary: The prince of Reuben in the wilderness, Elizur son of Shedeur, who stood with Moses and Aaron to number Israel, brought Reuben’s offering on the fourth day, and led Reuben’s host when the camp set out from Sinai (Num 1:5; 2:10; 7:30, 35; 10:18). It is אֵל “God” with the ־ִי of “my”, and צוּר “rock”: “my God is a rock”, the confession “who is God except Yahweh, and who is a rock except our God?” (2Sa 22:32), and of the Song of Moses, where the Rock is “a God of faithfulness” (Deu 32:4).

evidence.note: The standard of the camp of Reuben set out, “and over its host אֱלִיצוּר son of Shedeur”.
“For Reuben, אֱלִיצוּר son of Shedeur”, the first of the men to stand with Moses and Aaron.
Prince of the sons of Reuben, on the south side of the camp.
On the fourth day, the prince of the sons of Reuben (and 7:35, his offering).
“Who is אֵל except Yahweh, and who is a צוּר except our God?”: the name’s two words in one confession (Psa 18:32).
“The צוּר, his work is perfect … a God (אֵל) of faithfulness.”

note: BDB files the name under אֵל (a.dl.az, among the words of root אלה); it is linked here to the tsur entry for its second element, as Eliab is linked to av. The ־ִי may be “my” or a joining vowel (“God is a rock”). Its bearer is the son of Shedeur, שְׁדֵיאוּר “Shaddai is light”, and is listed beside Shelumiel son of צוּרִישַׁדָּי, “my rock is Shaddai” (Num 1:5–6).
